acceptance.assertion: Fresh evidence on the exact implementation base records the 94-entry compact bootstrap size, current warning and hard limits, startup project-request count, runtime-ready browser measurements and the current delivery architecture before any optimization; the previous 28,572-byte gzip bootstrap with only 100 bytes to the 28,672-byte warning threshold is treated as the motivating baseline, not silently rewritten.

At least one materially different catalog-startup architecture is implemented or measured against the current compact bootstrap using the same canonical 94-entry project truth. The decision records size, startup request behavior, runtime-ready impact, no-JavaScript recovery implications, implementation complexity and future catalog-growth behavior; simply raising the warning or hard limit does not satisfy this criterion.

The chosen design restores at least 2,048 gzip bytes of margin below the existing 28,672-byte compact-bootstrap warning threshold on the exact 94-entry tree, or replaces the linear bootstrap-size bottleneck with a bounded architecture whose fresh evidence demonstrates equivalent or stronger multi-batch growth reserve without moving the threshold. The 32,768-byte hard limit remains unchanged.

Public startup still performs zero per-project JSON requests, catalog intent search and initial discovery remain functional, and canonical catalog/projects/*.json files remain the source of project truth rather than generated bootstrap artifacts.

The bounded German and English no-JavaScript recovery pages remain complete and usable, all released locale overlays remain valid, and locale lifecycle/accessibility smoke evidence stays green without claiming native-speaker approval that was not performed.

Fresh catalog delivery budget, public browser smoke, low-power browser measurement, scale, recovery and hierarchy evidence are regenerated against the exact final tree and pass their existing contracts. No budget threshold is weakened to obtain a pass.

git diff --check and the complete repository validation suite pass on the exact final head; the full nontrivial PR diff receives a head-bound self-review, required GitHub CI is green on that head, merge is guarded against head drift, and successful Pages deployment plus production readback confirm the exact merged commit before closeout.

approval.note: The user explicitly instructed @grabowski on 2026-08-14 to implement the previously defined Commonworld bootstrap-headroom follow-up. goal: Restore material growth headroom in Commonworld's compact startup catalog before the next larger Commons batch, without weakening the existing delivery budget, reintroducing per-project startup fetches, or sacrificing the bounded DE/EN no-JavaScript recovery path. Compare the current bootstrap architecture with at least one materially different alternative, implement the smallest robust design that removes the immediate 100-byte warning-margin bottleneck, and bind the result to fresh delivery, browser, scale, recovery and hierarchy evidence.
